_note: These cutoffs are AlphaMissense's OWN PUBLISHED DEFAULTS, transcribed verbatim from the publisher's README (see source). They were NOT authored, chosen, or adjusted by the coding agent (control I3). A domain owner must confirm they are the right operating point for the ancestry-aware context, or supply different ones -- see DEFINITIONS.md sec 1 and docs/DEFINITIONS_QUESTIONNAIRE.md question A9. Sign-off flips status to SIGNED_OFF; until then the producer warns once per run.
_not_applied_here: The published files ship am_class already computed by the publisher, so the provider consumes the publisher's classification rather than re-deriving it from these numbers. The cutoffs are carried here so the rule is auditable and so a domain owner has something concrete to sign off on or override.
source: AlphaMissense README.md, Zenodo record 10.5281/zenodo.8208688, section 'Column descriptions' -> am_class; retrieved 2026-07-28
source_quote: 'likely_benign' if alphamissense_pathogenicity < 0.34; 'likely_pathogenic' if alphamissense_pathogenicity > 0.564; and 'ambiguous' otherwise

class_vocabularies._note: The publisher ships TWO label vocabularies for the SAME thresholds (verified against the real files, D-006). The provider normalizes both; neither is privileged.
